gen_risks.description: Neither MIPA nor the newly created ADISA have prior experience in implementing large donor-funded operations or World Bank fiduciary procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) with qualified finance specialists and provide continuous World Bank fiduciary training.
gen_risks.evidence: Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations

gen_risks.description: High procurement implementation risk due to ADISA being a newly created agency with an incomplete PMU setup.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists under the PPF, establish a detailed Project Operational Manual, and maintain Bank prior-review oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Since ADISA is a newly-created agency and the PMU is not yet fully set up, the procurement risk rating is high.

gen_risks.description: The ambitious and compressed reform timeline creates risks of implementation bottlenecks and delayed achievement of project targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Sequence reforms to balance quick wins with long-term structural changes, using DLI financial incentives and TA to sustain progress.
gen_risks.evidence: The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious.

gen_risks.description: Complex inter-sectoral coordination across more than a dozen participating government agencies may stall reform execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize the Prime Minister's Delivery Unit and Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee for high-level oversight and inter-agency coordination.
gen_risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

gen_risks.description: Civil servants and agency staff may resist relinquishing front-office functions to ADISA and new Citizen Service Centers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement comprehensive change management, communication programs, and stakeholder engagement to align incentives across civil service cadres.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC.

gen_risks.description: Incomplete digitization and missing national identification numbers in legacy property and pension registers hinder process re-engineering.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to digitize archives, optimize databases, and expand data exchange through the NAIS interoperability platform.
gen_risks.evidence: Property and pension records, for example, are only partially digitized.

gen_risks.description: Seven project institutions lack IT systems entirely, relying on manual paper processes that complicate workflow automation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phased development and deployment of basic document management, workflow, and decision-making IT systems tailored to each institution.
gen_risks.evidence: Seven institutions encompassed by the proposed project have no IT system in place.

gen_risks.description: Focusing on digital e-services and centralized urban service centers risks diminishing service access for poor, elderly, and rural populations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain existing regional access points, deploy assisted digital access outreach (internet cafes, municipal centers), and offer non-digital information channels.
gen_risks.evidence: there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery... will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable

gen_risks.description: Delays in drafting and passing Omnibus legislation may postpone the legal backing required for process re-engineering and license repeals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare process maps and legal inventories early through working groups and mobilize technical assistance for legal drafting.
gen_risks.evidence: Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation

gen_risks.description: Construction of the central Citizen Service Center building in Tirana causes environmental impacts such as noise, dust, waste, and traffic.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate the Environmental Management Plan (EMP) into bidding documents and construction contracts, ensuring continuous supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts that are associated with new construction include dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery on site

gen_risks.description: Unfunded ongoing operating costs, system licensing, and required periodic IT upgrades could compromise the sustainability of automated systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy PMU budget specialists to monitor annual appropriations and offset operating expenses with administrative efficiency savings.
gen_risks.evidence: Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance.

gen_risks.description: Service disruptions during front-office transitions could trigger public dissatisfaction if expectations are not managed effectively.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute targeted public communications campaigns and expand proactive citizen feedback mechanisms via SMS and call centers.
gen_risks.evidence: especially when some disruption in service may happen also, strong communication effort will have to be organized

gen_risks.description: Delays in approving the PPF and contracting key PMU staff threaten the timely commencement of project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Rely temporarily on MoF's CFCU for fiduciary support while re-advertising and expediting the recruitment of PMU specialists.
gen_risks.evidence: Except for the Financial Specialist, PMU staff are yet to be contracted due to the delay in the approval of the PPF.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
